answer: The Board should approve an appropriation of 1,470,000 US dollars for the Cycle 2025 Organizational Strengthening Grant line.
stakeholder_role: unstated in the prompt (writes the Board memo for a Kentucky community foundation pooled fund's grant line)

spine.entity: one exempt organization on the IRS Business Master File
spine.source: IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File, Kentucky cut (irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/eo_ky.csv), public domain; with the IRS SOI Form 990 and 990-EZ extracts FY2019 to FY2023 (27,785 returns)

world.org_type: pooled fund at a community foundation running a capacity-building grant line

driver: The decision is bounded by an eligible population assembled from a published source split into two archives with different field names, so the natural union nulls a third of the records silently while the closed-period back-test still passes, because every past award came from the archive the natural read keeps.
driver_concrete: The IRS publishes 990 and 990-EZ extracts as separate archives with different field names (totexpns against totfuncexpns, taxpd from FY2021), so a long-form-only panel finds 7 and 11 never-funded organizations in Bands 1 and 2, not 100 and 65; with Band 3 at 7 of 36 places the line needs 1,470,000 USD for 41 grants.
stump: A competent solver builds the screen from extracts read on the long form's column names, back-tests it against all five closed cycles (0 of 350 award bands change) and files 1,065,000 USD, never seeing that 9,944 short-form returns dropped out and 2,546 short-form filers left the population.

Several candidate measures reproduce their own year by arithmetic identity in sample, so only a held-out year separates them, and the contaminated measure's error grows in one direction.
